findings.evidence: Line 281 "Its field strength is the antisymmetric part of `B`" vs line 307 `Circle.exp (B v (x - y) - B (x - y) v)` described at line 302 as the flux of the field strength.
findings.fix: Write "its field strength is `F u w = B u w - B w u`" (or "twice the antisymmetric part of `B`") so both docstrings use one convention.
findings.issue: `ofBilin` docstring: "Its field strength is the antisymmetric part of `B`". With `A_ν(z) = B z e_ν`, `F_{μν} = ∂_μA_ν − ∂_νA_μ = B_{μν} − B_{νμ}`, which is twice the antisymmetric part; `pathLink_staple_ofBilin` (lines 302-304) calls the unhalved `B v (x-y) - B (x-y) v` the flux "of the field strength", so the two docstrings differ by a factor 2.

findings.evidence: Line 233 `def transverseLink (W : GaugeLink V G) (v x y : V) : G := W (x + v) (y + v)`; `(y + v) - (x + v) = y - x`; module docstring lines 41-44.
findings.fix: In both the module docstring and the `transverseLink` docstring, state the condition: the far segment carries the full separation `y - x` and is transverse exactly when `y - x` is (the physical transverse link being the `L → ∞` idealization).
findings.issue: `transverseLink v x y = W (x + v) (y + v)` is the link over the displacement `y - x`, which is transverse only when `y - x` is. The module docstring (lines 41-44) explicitly takes `n` to be the direction "along which the two quark fields are separated" and then calls this far segment "the transverse link", so under its own setup the rung is not transverse.

summary: Coverage is good and the module docstring is mathematical with no roadmap/process narrative, but two docstring claims are inaccurate: the field strength of `ofBilin` is off by a factor of two against the convention the same file's flux lemma uses, and the "transverse link" is not transverse in the setup the module docstring itself describes.
